questions.chapter: System Modeling, Transfer Functions & Block Diagram Algebra
questions.text: Define Open-Loop and Closed-Loop control systems with block diagrams and practical examples. Explain Transfer Function and its properties. Derive the closed-loop transfer function $\frac{C(s)}{R(s)} = \frac{G(s)}{1 + G(s)H(s)}$.

questions.chapter: System Modeling, Transfer Functions & Block Diagram Algebra
questions.text: Explain Block Diagram Reduction Rules (Moving summing points and takeoff points). Reduce a given complex multi-loop block diagram to find its overall transfer function $\frac{C(s)}{R(s)}$.

questions.chapter: System Modeling, Transfer Functions & Block Diagram Algebra
questions.text: State Mason's Gain Formula: $T = \frac{\sum P_k \Delta_k}{\Delta}$. Construct the Signal Flow Graph (SFG) for a given set of simultaneous differential/algebraic equations and calculate the overall transfer function.

questions.chapter: Time Response Analysis (Transient & Steady-State)
questions.text: Derive the unit step response of a standard Second-Order Underdamped Control System ($0 < \zeta < 1$): $c(t) = 1 - \frac{e^{-\zeta\omega_n t}}{\sqrt{1-\zeta^2}}\sin(\omega_d t + \theta)$. Define and derive formulas for: (a) Delay Time ($t_d$), (b) Rise Time ($t_r = \frac{\pi-\theta}{\omega_d}$), (c) Peak Time ($t_p = \frac{\pi}{\omega_d}$), (d) Maximum Percentage Overshoot ($M_p = e^{-\frac{\pi\zeta}{\sqrt{1-\zeta^2}}} \times 100\%$), and (e) Settling Time ($t_s = \frac{4}{\zeta\omega_n}$ for $2\%$ criterion).

questions.chapter: Time Response Analysis (Transient & Steady-State)
questions.text: Define Steady-State Error ($e_{ss}$) and Static Error Constants: Positional Error Constant ($K_p = \lim_{s\to 0} G(s)H(s)$), Velocity Error Constant ($K_v = \lim_{s\to 0} s G(s)H(s)$), and Acceleration Error Constant ($K_a = \lim_{s\to 0} s^2 G(s)H(s)$). Construct the steady-state error table for Type 0, Type 1, and Type 2 systems subjected to unit step, ramp, and parabolic inputs.

questions.chapter: Stability Analysis (Routh-Hurwitz Criterion)
questions.text: State the Routh-Hurwitz Stability Criterion. Explain Special Cases in Routh's array: (1) First element of any row becomes zero with non-zero elements remaining ($\epsilon$-method and $s = 1/z$ substitution), and (2) An entire row of zeros (Auxiliary polynomial $A(s)$ and its derivative). Determine the range of parameter $K$ for stability of the characteristic equation: $s^4 + 2s^3 + (4+K)s^2 + 9s + 25 = 0$.

questions.chapter: Root Locus Technique & Frequency Response (Bode & Nyquist)
questions.text: State all Rules for constructing the Root Locus: Starting/ending points, Number of branches, Symmetry about real axis, Asymptotes angle ($\theta_a = \frac{(2q+1)180^\circ}{P-Z}$), Centroid ($\sigma_a = \frac{\sum P - \sum Z}{P-Z}$), Breakaway and Break-in points ($\frac{dK}{ds} = 0$), Angle of departure/arrival, and imaginary axis crossing using Routh array. Sketch the root locus for $G(s)H(s) = \frac{K}{s(s+2)(s^2+4s+13)}$ and find the marginal value of $K$ for stability.

questions.chapter: Root Locus Technique & Frequency Response (Bode & Nyquist)
questions.text: Define Gain Margin (GM) and Phase Margin (PM). Draw the asymptotic Bode Magnitude and Phase plots for the open-loop transfer function: $G(s) = \frac{100(s+2)}{s(s+10)(s+50)}$. From the Bode plot, determine the Gain Crossover Frequency ($\omega_{gc}$), Phase Crossover Frequency ($\omega_{pc}$), Gain Margin, and Phase Margin.

questions.chapter: Root Locus Technique & Frequency Response (Bode & Nyquist)
questions.text: State the Nyquist Stability Criterion ($N = P - Z$). Sketch the Nyquist Contour and Nyquist Plot for $G(s)H(s) = \frac{K}{(s+1)(s+2)(s+3)}$ and determine the stability of the closed-loop system for $K = 10$ and $K = 100$.

questions.chapter: State-Space Analysis & Compensator Design (Lead, Lag, PID)
questions.text: Explain State-Space Representation of continuous LTI systems: $\dot{\mathbf{x}}(t) = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}(t) + \mathbf{B}u(t)$, $y(t) = \mathbf{C}\mathbf{x}(t) + \mathbf{D}u(t)$. Derive the State Transition Matrix: $\boldsymbol{\Phi}(t) = e^{\mathbf{A}t} = \mathcal{L}^{-1}\{(s\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{A})^{-1}\}$. Find $\boldsymbol{\Phi}(t)$ for $\mathbf{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$.

questions.chapter: State-Space Analysis & Compensator Design (Lead, Lag, PID)
questions.text: Define Controllability and Observability. State Kalman's Controllability Test (Rank of $\mathbf{Q}_c = [\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{A}\mathbf{B}, \dots, \mathbf{A}^{n-1}\mathbf{B}]$) and Observability Test (Rank of $\mathbf{Q}_o = [\mathbf{C}^T, \mathbf{A}^T\mathbf{C}^T, \dots, (\mathbf{A}^T)^{n-1}\mathbf{C}^T]$).

questions.chapter: State-Space Analysis & Compensator Design (Lead, Lag, PID)
questions.text: Compare Lead Compensator, Lag Compensator, and Lag-Lead Compensator in terms of frequency response, phase shift, bandwidth, and transient/steady-state performance. Explain PID Controller tuning using the Ziegler-Nichols method.
